Answer within 10 s, credited to Medicare.gov fact sheet 12234: no, the $50 a month doesn't count toward your Part D deductible or yearly out-of-pocket limit. package.title: Does Medicare's $50 Wegovy or Zepbound Pen Count Toward Your Cap? #shorts
package.description:
Follow @InforMedLab for more on the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: who qualifies.

If you qualify, the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge (July 1, 2026 to Dec 31, 2027) charges $50 a month for weight-management Wegovy injection or tablet, Foundayo tablet or Zepbound KwikPen — but Medicare says it doesn't count toward your Part D deductible or yearly out-of-pocket cap. Common side effects: nausea and diarrhea. Don't switch or stop medicines on your own.

#Medicare #GLP1 #Wegovy #Zepbound #PartD

factcheck.summary: The core claims check out. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge charges a $50 copay and runs from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027. The program covers Foundayo, Wegovy injection and tablet, and the Zepbound KwikPen only; Zepbound single-dose vials and single-dose pens are excluded (confirmed on the CMS provider page). The CMS provider page confirms that type 2 diabetes, moderate-to-severe OSA and noncirrhotic MASH are covered through Part D instead, as are prescriptions written to reduce the risk of major heart events (MACE). Several outlets (KFF Health News, AARP, NPR), plus search snippets of the Medicare.gov fact sheet, say the $50 does not count toward the Part D deductible or the yearly out-of-pocket limit. The fact sheet PDF itself couldn't be read as text, but its URL resolves on Medicare.gov. Medicare.gov confirms Open Enrollment runs Oct 15 to Dec 7. MedlinePlus lists nausea and diarrhea for both tirzepatide and semaglutide. The safety lines, prescriber line, no-switching line and conditional funnel CTA are all present. Only minor scope and wording fixes remain.

issues.problem: The CMS source covers only noncirrhotic MASH. The on-screen list says 'no cirrhosis' but the narration doesn't, so the spoken line is broader than the source.
issues.fix: Type two diabetes, moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea, or the liver disease MASH without cirrhosis? Or prescribed to lower heart attack and stroke risk? You may be covered through your regular drug plan instead.

issues.problem: This reads as if the Bridge itself has a Dec 7 deadline. Dec 7 is when Part D/Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment ends for 2027 plan changes. The Bridge runs to Dec 31, 2027 and has no such deadline. The retention note 'this week' is also inaccurate.
issues.fix: on_screen_text: "Open Enrollment Ends Dec 7, 2026"; stat_label: "Medicare Open Enrollment (Oct 15 to Dec 7) ends; plan changes start Jan 1, 2027"; narration: "Medicare open enrollment runs through December seventh, twenty twenty-six. Ask your plan and prescriber how your costs work."

issues.problem: 'It' is ambiguous after the s4 list. The program is never named aloud.
issues.fix: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge runs July first, twenty twenty-six, to December thirty-first, twenty twenty-seven. Now the part most people miss.

issues.claim: "Wegovy injection or tablet, Foundayo tablet, and Zepbound KwikPen only."
issues.problem: The narration leaves out that Bridge coverage applies only to weight-management prescriptions for eligible Part D enrollees who meet the BMI criteria. A muted or partial viewer could read it as general coverage.
issues.fix: For weight management, if you qualify: Wegovy injection or tablet, Foundayo tablet, and Zepbound KwikPen only. Not Zepbound vials or the single-dose pen.

issues.problem: The URL resolves, but the June 2026 date couldn't be confirmed from the PDF text.
issues.fix: Use title "Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: GLP-1 Drugs for $50 a Month (CMS Product No. 12234)" unless the revision date printed in the PDF is confirmed.
